# Effective diffusion coefficients from a binary matrix

`eos.effective_diffusion`

## Source

**NeqSim master `Diffusivity`**

`calcEffectiveDiffusionCoefficients`, the same eight lines in `commonphasephysicalproperties/diffusivity/Diffusivity` and in `liquidphysicalproperties/diffusivity/Diffusivity`.


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `binary_diffusion` | m**2/s | the pair coefficients, **row-major and not symmetric**. `D_ij` is the coefficient of component `i` at infinite dilution in `j`; only row `i` is read for `D_eff_i`. |
| `x` | dimensionless | the phase's mole fractions. Every other component's fraction divides its pair coefficient, so this is the composition the effective coefficients are for. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `effective_diffusion` | m**2/s | each component's effective coefficient, in the same order as `x`. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `x >= 0` | raises | a mole fraction cannot be negative; the class does not check it, and a negative one silently subtracts from a sum |

## Assumptions

- **the assembly is eight lines and this is all of it**: `D_eff_i = (1 - x_i) / sum_{j != i} x_j / D_ij`, over one row of the binary matrix per component. `PhysicalProperties.calcEffectiveDiffusionCoefficients` delegates to the diffusivity model, and every model in the family writes the same loop.
- **the binary matrix is the diffusivity model's, and it is an input.** Its entries are `calcBinaryDiffusionCoefficient(i, j, method)`, whose live model on a liquid phase is `SiddiqiLucasMethod` - the coefficient `eos.siddiqi_lucas_diffusivity` carries.
- **the assembly reads the matrix directly, not the Fick getter.** `getFickBinaryDiffusionCoefficient` on a liquid phase multiplies the entry by a Maxwell-Stefan correction, so with the derivative uninitialised it returns a diagonal - which a first reading mistook for the matrix.
- **the matrix is not symmetric**: `D_ij` and `D_ji` are different numbers, because each is the infinite-dilution coefficient of one substance in the other. Row `i` alone decides `D_eff_i`, so an asymmetric matrix is the normal case and not a defect.
- **fewer than two components is refused.** NeqSim divides `(1 - x_i)` by an empty sum there, so it returns a NaN; a phase with one substance has no effective diffusion coefficient and this refuses rather than reporting one.
- `x` is checked (non-negative) rather than renormalised, and the sum is over every other component's fraction, so a composition that does not sum to one gives an answer that does not mean one.

## Cases

| Case | Inputs | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `co2_water_aqueous_phase` | binary_diffusion = [[1.3298101098167177e-07, 1.32981826012159e-07], [1.329826410361882e-07, 2.0568595403496719e-07]], x = [1.4052475102269458e-05, 0.9999859475248978] | effective_diffusion = [1.32981826012159e-07, 1.3298264103573872e-07] |
| `methane_n_heptane_oil_phase` | binary_diffusion = [[1.4366530998185989e-07, 1.432289958431809e-07], [1.427958072195365e-07, 6.89737792946623e-08]], x = [0.004145278302387163, 0.9958547216976128] | effective_diffusion = [1.432289958431809e-07, 1.4279580721953783e-07] |

## References

- NeqSim - https://github.com/equinor/neqsim - Apache-2.0. `PhysicalProperties.calcEffectiveDiffusionCoefficients` and `Diffusivity.calcEffectiveDiffusionCoefficients` are the port source.
- Fuller, E. N.; Schettler, P. D.; Giddings, J. C. (1966). "A new method for prediction of binary gas-phase diffusion coefficients." Industrial & Engineering Chemistry 58(5), 18-27. The pair-coefficient form the binary matrix is assembled from.
- `validation/neqsim/EffectiveDiffusionProbe.java` and `captures/effective_diffusion_probe.tsv` - the capture, which holds the matrix, the vector and the vector recomputed from the matrix.
